placements.title: Test cases are built to reproduce real production failure modes and assert the fix holds under them, not just to verify intended behavior
placements.frame: Does this expression name a real production failure being deliberately reproduced as a test case, and what invariant (non-crashing, valid output) is being asserted to prevent its recurrence?
placements.why: Both segments describe one test case unit: src-1 states the test reproduces a specific known production failure pattern (missing-id, ## heading without id field), and src-2 states the required invariant the fix must satisfy (no crash, valid slug produced). Together they instantiate a recurring engineering theme — regression coverage derived directly from a real production incident, with an explicit robustness invariant — that future envelopes describing other derive-id or pipeline test cases will keep feeding; it is a directional subject about how testing is done here, not a one-time fact. No existing graph structure or strata was supplied (both empty for this repo) and the only loaded perspective material (ns__Decision_DiagnosticFirst, an engagement-methodology decision under ns__Strategy) does not plausibly cover id-derivation, markdown parsing, slug generation, or production-failure-driven testing, so nothing exact or inspired-adjacent exists to reuse or extend. Minting standalone is the legible move for a first-content, empty-graph situation.
